cites.quote: On 24 February the newly elected Knesset held its first session.

reaction.policy: Only dated institutional steps; leader reactions require all seated lists or none.
reaction.gap: Election-night statements were not collected for all lists; none is selected.

cites.quote: Of all 12 factions, only Kadima, with its 28 MKs, recommended that Peres designate Kadima leader Tzipi Livni to form the next government. The Likud, Habayit Hayehudi, Israel Beiteinu, Shas, National Union and United Torah Judaism (a total of 65 MKs) recommended that the mandate be given to Likud chairman Binyamin Netanyahu, while Meretz, Balad, Labor, Hadash and the United Arab List-Ta'al refrained from recommending anyone.

As of Thursday, 65 Knesset members have recommended Netanyahu, including the religious parties, while Livni has received only the nomination of her own party. The left-wing Meretz Party did not nominate a candidate

זאת לאחר ש-65 חברי כנסת המליצו בפני הנשיא על נתניהו כמי שראוי להטיל עליו את הרכבת הממשלה, לעומת 28 חברי כנסת (ממפלגתה בלבד), שהמליצו על ציפי לבני, ולאחר שמפלגת העבודה החליטה שלא להמליץ על אף אחד מחברי הכנסת

notes: Consultations were held on 18–19 February 2009; the date is the last consultation day. President Peres tasked Netanyahu on 20 February 2009. Party-by-party positions are from the Jerusalem Post report of 19 February 2009; Hebrew Wikipedia is kept as a secondary source.

events.textEn: Peres tasked Benjamin Netanyahu with forming a government for 28 days.
events.textHe: פרס הטיל על בנימין נתניהו להרכיב ממשלה בתוך 28 ימים.

cites.quote: entrusted him with the task of forming a government. Netanyahu now has 28 days

events.textEn: Peres granted Netanyahu a two-week extension, until 3 April.
events.textHe: פרס העניק לנתניהו הארכה של שבועיים, עד 3 באפריל.

cites.quote: won a two-week extension on Friday to form a government
The extension sets April 3 as his new deadline.

events.textEn: The Knesset approved the 32nd government, 69–45, with five abstentions; the ministers were sworn in.
events.textHe: הכנסת הביעה אמון בממשלה ה־32 ברוב של 69 מול 45, וחמישה נמנעים; השרים הושבעו.

cites.quote: a vote of 69 to 45 with five abstentions.

events.textEn: Gilad Shalit was released from captivity in Gaza in a prisoner exchange between Israel and Hamas.
events.textHe: גלעד שליט שוחרר מהשבי ברצועת עזה בעסקת חילופי אסירים בין ישראל לחמאס.

cites.quote: On 18 October 2011, Gilad Shalit an Israeli soldier
The exchange of prisoners starts on 18 October.
Shalit is finally freed over five years later in a prisoner exchange.

events.textEn: Israel launched Operation Pillar of Defense against Gaza terrorist organizations after rocket attacks on Israeli civilians; a ceasefire was announced on 21 November 2012.
events.textHe: ישראל פתחה במבצע עמוד ענן נגד ארגוני טרור בעזה בעקבות ירי רקטות על אזרחים בישראל; הפסקת אש הוכרזה ב־21 בנובמבר 2012.

cites.quote: with the objective of reducing the number of rocket attacks at Israeli civilians.
Ahmed Jabari, Hamas’s top military commander.
a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas is announced on 21 November
Israel kills Hamas's military chief of staff, Ahmad Jabari

notes: During the 32nd government’s caretaker tenure, after the October dissolution.

The IDF operation history supplies the Israeli name and rocket-attack context; the inherited independent chronology pair remains the selection evidence. The date field gives the launch; endDate records the cited ceasefire, not a peace treaty.

The IDF dates the launch to 14 November 2012, beginning with the killing of Hamas terrorist commander Ahmed Jabari; Hamas and other terrorist organizations fired rockets at Israel during the operation.
צה״ל מתארך את תחילת המבצע ל־14 בנובמבר 2012, עם הריגת מפקד הטרור של חמאס אחמד ג׳עברי; חמאס וארגוני טרור נוספים ירו רקטות לעבר ישראל במהלך המבצע.

endedBy.textEn: The Knesset voted to dissolve itself, 100–0, and set an election for 22 January 2013.
endedBy.textHe: הכנסת הצביעה על התפזרותה ברוב של 100 ללא מתנגדים וקבעה בחירות ל־22 בינואר 2013.

cites.quote: Date of dissolution of the outgoing legislature: 15 October 2012
One hundred MKs voted in favor, with no opposing votes and zero abstentions

notes: 15 October is the IPU/sitting date and the date on the ToI report. Reports published after midnight on 16 October describe the same vote; exact civil-time/Gazette date not verified.
